investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the allocatable VM slots on those nodes are fully consumed. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, so preemption was also not possible. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the allocatable VM slots on those nodes are fully consumed. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, so preemption was also not possible. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod created by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so no pod could be scheduled and no agent was ever created, leaving the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. The eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), which submits a pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm. With 0/6 nodes schedulable — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — the pod remains pending until the eval times out. Because the agent pod never starts, no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is ever collected, and the expected-output contract is fully violated. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have claimed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements (e.g., a label or taint restricting remote agent pods to kata/peer-pod capable nodes), reducing the schedulable node count to 2 and amplifying the capacity shortage.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or a production workload may have created remote agent pods that were not cleaned up (leaked), consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that would otherwise be available to the eval. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) is intended to prevent this, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

Lower confidence — the cluster may have been scaled down or nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm support may have been cordoned or removed, reducing total VM capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run. No node-event evidence is present to confirm this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the scheduler message were absent or different (e.g., an API authentication error or a timeout from a running pod), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would not apply.

If kubectl describe node showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling constraint would need to be identified.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all 5 required evidence fields, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that failed due to affinity/selector mismatch were found to also carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but were excluded by a misconfigured node selector or affinity rule, the primary cause would shift from resource exhaustion to a scheduling configuration error.

If no pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the cluster at the time of failure, the cause would shift to a node-level issue (e.g., nodes cordoned, kata runtime not installed, or extended resource not advertised by the device plugin).
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure signal rather than a timeout failure.
Add an eval that counts currently running remote agent pods in the cluster and alerts if the count is unexpectedly high (potential leak detection).

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are in a schedulable state, catching node cordon or pool shrink events before they impact agent evals.

Consider adding a cleanup-verification eval that confirms the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs successfully terminated all pods created during a prior eval run, to detect leaked resources early.
